head: 14bac80
target: Repos opt into the gate with a committed marker file instead of each clone pointing git at a hooks directory.
incidental: the selftest script moved out of the skill directory
SKILL.md wording for the new opt-in flow
agent-mode.md wording on spawning fresh examiners

questions.prompt: Before this change, each clone needed a git setting to find its hooks. Why does opt-in now live in a file you commit?

options.label: Fresh clones carry the opt-in, so no one repeats a manual setup step
Git refuses to run hooks until a tracked file opts the repo in
A committed file lets the gate edit git settings in every clone
A committed file stores the repo's quiz results for everyone to share

key_points: the old opt-in was a setting inside one clone, so it never traveled to a fresh clone
a committed file carries the opt-in into every clone of the repo
so no fresh clone needs a manual setup step before the gate works

questions.prompt: Why does the hook run the gate from a stable path on your machine, not from the plugin's install directory?

options.label: The plugin's install path changes with every update, so the hook would break
Git refuses to run a hook that points at a file outside the repository
Files inside the plugin directory cannot be marked executable for other programs
The plugin directory is erased at the end of every session

key_points: the plugin's install path changes with every update
a hook pointing there would break or run a stale gate
the stable copy is refreshed each session, so the hook keeps working

questions.prompt: A developer clones the opted-in repo and never uses the plugin. What does the committed marker file enforce there?

options.label: Nothing; the marker is a signal, and the plugin installs the enforcing hook
It rewrites the clone's git settings to point at the hook
It asks the remote to reject pushes that lack a passed quiz
It blocks the first push until the developer runs the gate

key_points: the marker is only a signal; it enforces nothing by itself
enforcement is the push hook, which only the plugin installs
a clone that never runs the plugin has no gate at all

questions.prompt: A teammate starts a session in a fresh clone of an opted-in repo. Which of these does the plugin's session-start command do?

options.label: It writes the push hook into the clone's own hooks directory
It refreshes the gate copy at the stable path, if it changed
It rewrites the committed marker file with the session's date
It points the clone's git settings at a tracked hooks directory

key_points: the hook is written into the clone's own hooks directory
the gate copy at the stable path is refreshed when it changed
nothing tracked in the repo changes, and no git settings are touched

questions.prompt: The hook runs, but the gate tool is missing from the machine. What happens to the push?

options.label: The push is blocked, with a message pointing to how to install the gate
The push goes through, since no gate means nothing to enforce
The push waits until the gate is installed
Git skips the broken hook with a warning

key_points: the gate fails closed: a missing tool blocks the push
the hook prints where to get the gate, so the user is not stuck

questions.prompt: A repo already has a pre-push hook its author wrote by hand. What does the session-start command do?

options.label: It leaves the hook alone and says which line to add by hand
It replaces the hook with the gate's own version
It appends the gate check to the author's hook
It renames the author's hook and installs its own beside it

key_points: the gate never overwrites a hook it did not write
the author keeps their hook and adds the check line themselves
when the gate's own hook is already there, the command changes nothing

questions.prompt: The gate gains a new check. How do clones that already have the installed hook pick it up?

options.label: Into the gate tool; the session command refreshes the copy the hook calls
Into every installed hook; the session command rewrites them
Into the committed marker file; clones read it at push time
Into a new hook template; users must reinstall by hand

key_points: the installed hook is a thin wrapper that only finds and runs the gate
the rules live in the gate copy at the stable path
refreshing that copy is enough; clones pick up new rules without reinstalling

questions.prompt: A repo adopts the gate; its author has a pre-push hook, and a teammate never uses the plugin. What does each of them get?
key_points: the repo opts in with one committed marker file
the author's hook is kept, and the message names the line to add
the teammate's pushes are not gated, because only the plugin installs the hook
plugin users get the gate with no manual step
